page: Microsoft Azure D4lds_v5 is a compute-optimized virtual machine belonging to the DLDSv5 family. It is built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz. The server features 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. It is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core. For local storage, the instance includes a bundled 154 GB SSD. It operates under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and does not include any GPU hardware or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals moderate single-core performance alongside weaker multi-core and memory capabilities. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance and Geekbench single-core score both rank in the average tier. However, multi-core execution is constrained, with the Geekbench multi-core score and stress-ng multi-core performance falling into the weak category. Memory performance is a notable bottleneck; the Passmark memory score and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression are rated as poor. Large block memory read bandwidth is limited to 30.07 GB/sec, though write bandwidth remains average at 26.03 GB/sec.

The D4lds_v5 offers a specific tradeoff between dedicated compute resources and memory capacity. While the inclusion of a 154 GB local SSD provides fast local storage, the low memory-to-vCPU ratio limits its suitability for memory-intensive applications. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the server provides dedicated Intel Xeon execution threads at a lower memory footprint, making it a viable option for workloads that require CPU cycles but do not demand large RAM allocations. It is best suited for lightweight web serving, single-threaded file compression tasks, and basic text processing, but is poorly suited for database operations, software compilation, or multi-threaded decompression.
description: Microsoft Azure D4lds_v5 is a compute-optimized virtual machine from the DLDSv5 family, featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs and 8.0 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor at 2.8 GHz, it includes a 154 GB local SSD and operates under Microsoft Hyper-V. The server exhibits average single-core performance, as shown by its Geekbench single-core score of 1654.0, but is constrained in multi-core and memory-bound tasks. Multi-core stress-ng and Passmark memory benchmarks fall into the weak and poor categories, respectively. With a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB, this instance presents a clear tradeoff, prioritizing dedicated CPU allocation over memory capacity. It is qualitatively cost-effective for CPU-bound tasks with low memory footprints, making it suitable for static web serving, basic text processing, and lightweight single-threaded workloads, while remaining less optimal for memory-intensive databases or complex software compilation.
